### 6.18.2 Investigating Events

Event sequence data are given as a list of column groups, one per
sequence data structure – the manual’s `seq8.cf` defines two from
`seq.d4`, `Y0..Y5` and `S0..S5`.
[`tda_seqev()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_seqmd.md)
counts the events (Box 3), and
[`tda_seqevd()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_seqmd.md)
their distribution over time for the first structure (Box 4).

Box 176seq_info, seqev and seqevd

``` r
seqd4 <- read.table(ex("seq.d4"))
names(seqd4) <- c("ID", paste0("Y", 0:5), paste0("S", 0:5), "V1", "V2")
multi <- list(paste0("Y", 0:5), paste0("S", 0:5))

tda_seq_info(multi, data = seqd4)
```

      sn type variables tmin tmax nstates states
    1  1    1         6    0    5       2   1, 2
    2  2    1         6    0    5       2   1, 3

``` r
tda_seqev(multi, data = seqd4)
```

      from to count
    1    1  2     4
    2    2  1     3

``` r
tda_seqevd(multi, data = seqd4)
```

      time cases ev1_2 ev2_1 total
    1    1     3     1     0     1
    2    2     3     1     2     3
    3    3     3     0     0     0
    4    4     3     1     1     2
    5    5     3     1     0     1

### 6.18.3 Data Generation

[`tda_seqmd()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_seqmd.md)
turns sequences into episode data around chosen events, which is how a
sequence becomes something a rate model can take.

``` r
tda_seqmd(paste0("Y", 0:5), event = c(1, 2), data = seqd4, summary = TRUE)
```

`xe=` adds time-varying covariates derived from a date: `xe=[V1],[V2]`
(the manual’s `seq8c.cf`, Box 4) gives, for each episode, the process
time since the date each variable holds – `event_covariates=`, named
after the columns TDA writes.

Box 178seqmd with xe= (seq8c.cf)

``` r
tda_seqmd(paste0("Y", 0:5), event = c(1, 2), data = seqd4,
           covariates = c("V1", "V2"),
           event_covariates = list(V1_D = "V1", V2_D = "V2"))
```

      id time event period1 period2 period3 period4 period5 V1  V2 V1_D V2_D

    9  3    4     1       0       0       0       1       0  2 -20    2   24

A third form of `xe=` counts the events of a given type in another
sequence structure before the present time and the time since the last
one, with effect-shape dummies (`seq8d.cf`, the manual’s Box 5):
`[1,2,1,4]` is the event 1 -\> 2 in structure 1, with 4 dummies.

Box 179seqmd with event counting (seq8d.cf)

``` r
tda_seqmd(paste0("Y", 0:5), event = c(1, 2), data = seqd4,
           covariates = c("V1", "V2"),
           event_covariates = list(V1_D = "V1", V2_D = "V2"),
           options = list(xe = "[V1],[V2],[1,2,1,4]"))
```

### 6.19.2 Loglinear Models

`ll2.dat` carries a fourth column, `S`, the scale factors of 6.19.1’s
structural zeros; `ll2.cf` defines it and does not use it, and the
residual table’s `Scale` column is all ones accordingly. `scale=` would
pass it.

Box 181A loglinear model with residuals

``` r
ll2 <- read.table(ex("ll2.dat"), col.names = c("X1", "X2", "F", "S"))
fit <- tda_loglin(~ X1 + X2, data = ll2, weights = "F", residuals = TRUE)
fit
```

## 7 Relational Data

### 7.2.1.1 Degree of Nodes

`gni` reports each node of the current graph: its number, its label, and
per value variable the in-degree, out-degree and number of loops.
`gd4.cf` runs it on `gd1.dat`, which defines two graphs.

Box 182gni (gd4.cf)

``` r
gd1n <- read.table(ex("gd1.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V1", "V2"))
tda_g_nodes(tda_graph(gd1n, directed = TRUE))$table
```

      V1 V2 V3 V4 V5 V6 V7 V8
    1  1  1  1  2  0  2  0  0
    2  2  5  1  0  0  0  1  0
    3  3  7  1  1  0  1  1  0
    4  4  8  0  0  1  0  1  0
    5  5  9  0  0  0  0  0  0
    6  6 11  0  1  0  1  0  0
    7  7 12  1  0  0  0  1  0

Node 8’s first-graph degrees read 0 and 0 here; the manual’s box prints
1 and 1. Running `gd4.cf` through TDA gives 0 and 0, and so does a build
of Rohwer’s unmodified sources, so the box is out of date.

Chapter 7 is relational data. The manual’s example graph is `gd1.dat`:
an edge list `I, J` with two value variables, `V1` and `V2`, so every
node count comes once per value variable.
[`tda_graph()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_graph.md)
is the `gdd` command and
[`tda_g_degrees()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gni`. A loop (node 8 to itself) is counted in its own column and not
in the degrees; the manual’s Box 1 (2002) counted it in both, TDA 6.4p
does not.

Box 183gni: in-degree, out-degree and loops per value variable (gd4.cf)

``` r
gd1 <- read.table(ex("gd1.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V1", "V2"))
g1 <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = TRUE)
tda_g_degrees(g1)
```

      index node in_degree1 out_degree1 loops1 in_degree2 out_degree2 loops2 degree
    1     1    1          1           2      0          2           0      0      3
    2     2    5          1           0      0          0           1      0      1
    3     3    7          1           1      0          1           1      0      2
    4     4    8          0           0      1          0           1      0      0
    5     5    9          0           0      0          0           0      0      0
    6     6   11          0           1      0          1           0      0      1
    7     7   12          1           0      0          0           1      0      1

[`tda_g_links()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)

node with any forward links.

``` r
tda_g_links(g1)$table                     # forward links
```

``` r
tda_g_links(g1, backward = TRUE)$table    # and backward
```

### 7.2.2.1 Topological Sorting

[`tda_g_toposort()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gsort`, on the manual’s `gd6.dat`: a directed acyclic graph, its
nodes in an order that respects every edge.

Box 185gsort (gd22.cf)

``` r
gd6 <- read.table(ex("gd6.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
gsrt <- tda_graph(gd6, directed = TRUE)
tda_g_toposort(gsrt)$table
```

    5 5      7       3

``` r
# option 2 relabels the graph's edges, keeping their values
tda_g_toposort(gsrt, relabel_graph = TRUE)$table
```

### 7.2.3.1 Connected Components

[`tda_g_components()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gcon`. `gd7.cf` declares `gd1.dat` undirected and valued (`gt = 2`)
and asks for the components of its second graph, the one `V2` defines
(`gn = 2`): node 8 joins component 1 through the edge 8-7 that `V2`
carries and `V1` does not.

Box 186gcon: components of graph 2 (gd7.cf)

``` r
gcomp <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = FALSE)
tda_g_components(gcomp, gn = 2)$table
```

      component n i node_i
    1         1 4 1      1
    2         1 4 2      5
    3         1 4 3      7
    4         1 4 4      8
    5         2 1 5      9
    6         3 2 6     11
    7         3 2 7     12

``` r
# option 2 lists each component's edges instead, with their values
tda_g_components(gcomp, gn = 2, edges = TRUE)$table
```

      component n i j node_i node_j value
    1         1 4 1 2      1      5     4
    2         1 4 1 3      1      7    15
    3         1 4 3 4      7      8     0
    4         2 1 5 5      9      9    -1
    5         3 2 6 7     11     12    14

### 7.2.3.2 Reachable Nodes in Directed Graphs

`gdcon` (`tda_g(g, "gdcon")`) is the directed counterpart of `gcon`:
strongly connected components (`opt = 1`) or, with `opt = 2`, the nodes
each node reaches. `gd8.cf` runs it on graph 2 of `gd1.dat`.

Box 187gdcon: reachable nodes (gd8.cf) (gd30.cf)

``` r
g1d <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = TRUE)
tda_g(g1d, "gdcon", list(gn = 2, opt = 2))$table
```

    4 records, lengths 4-5
    [1]  2 5 1 1 
    [2]  3 7 1 1 
    [3]  4 8 2 1 7 
    [4]   7 12  1 11 

### 7.2.3.3 Cut Nodes and Blocks

[`tda_g_cutpoints()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gcut`, on `gd8.dat`: the nodes whose removal disconnects the graph,
and with `opt = 2` the blocks.

Box 188gcut (gd26.cf)

``` r
gd8 <- read.table(ex("gd8.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
g8 <- tda_graph(gd8, directed = FALSE)
tda_g_cutpoints(g8)$table
```

    [2]  2 3 0

``` r
tda_g_cutpoints(g8, opt = 2)$table
```

### 7.2.4.1 Enumeration of Paths

[`tda_g_paths()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gep`, on `gd5.dat`, a small directed graph; `gd20.cf` runs its six
output options: the paths between all pairs of nodes, their number per
pair, the shortest and longest path per pair, and the two full listings
with each path’s length and value.

``` r
gd5 <- read.table(ex("gd5.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
g5 <- tda_graph(gd5, directed = TRUE)
for (o in 1:6)
    print(tda_g_paths(g5, opt = o)$table)
```

``` r
p <- tda_ps(xlim = c(0, 8), ylim = c(-1, 5), width = 80, height = 40)

                    curve = c(-3, 0, -3, -3, 0, 0, -3, 0, -3),

                    arrow = "1.5,1.0")
plot(tda_pl_graph(p, nodes, edges))
```

``` r
# gdd's gt= is the graph type: 1 undirected unvalued, 2 undirected
```

### 7.2.6.1 Fundamental Set of Cycles

[`tda_g_cycles()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_g_analyses.md)
is `gcyc`; `gd30.cf` runs it on `gd9.dat`, an undirected graph with 6
nodes and 11 edges. `opt = 1` lists a fundamental set of cycles, one
ragged record each: index, cycle number, length, and the nodes.

`gcyc`’s four options are four views of the same cycle space. Option 1
lists the nodes of each fundamental cycle, so its rows are ragged;
option 2 gives the edge and one indicator per fundamental cycle; option
3 the same over every cycle found; option 4 writes the edges first and
then one indicator row per cycle, two row shapes in the one file, which
is why it arrives ragged as well.

Box 199gcyc, options 1 to 4

``` r
gd9 <- read.table(ex("gd9.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
g9 <- tda_graph(gd9, directed = FALSE)
tda_g_cycles(g9, "fundamental_nodes")$table
```

    [2]  1 2 5 6 1 2 
    [3]  1 3 5 6 4 
    [4]  1 4 4 6 1 2 
    [5]  1 5 4 6 1 3 
    [6]  1 6 3 1 2

``` r
tda_g_cycles(g9, "fundamental_edges")$table
```

### 7.3.1.1 The Linear Assignment Problem

[`tda_gap()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_gap.md) is
`gap`: given a cost matrix, the assignment of rows to columns with
minimal total cost. The manual’s `co1.dat` is a 6 x 6 cost matrix, row
by row; the result is the permutation of its Box 2 and the matrix with
its rows permuted accordingly.

Box 209gap (co1.cf)

``` r
cost <- matrix(scan(ex("co1.dat"), quiet = TRUE), 6, 6, byrow = TRUE)
ap <- tda_gap(cost)
ap$assignment
```

    [2,]    2    4
    [3,]    3    3
    [4,]    4    1
    [5,]    5    5
    [6,]    6    2


### 7.3.1.2 The Quadratic Assignment Problem

[`tda_gqap()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_gqap.md) is
`gqap`, on two symmetric matrices, a flow and a distance matrix.
`co2.dat` gives their lower triangles in one file, one pair per line in
the order (2,1), (3,1), (3,2); the manual’s Box 2 is the permutation 2,
1, 3.

Box 210gqap (co2.cf)

``` r
co2 <- read.table(ex("co2.dat"), col.names = c("F", "D"))
lower <- function(v) { m <- matrix(0, 3, 3); m[lower.tri(m)] <- v; m + t(m) }
qap <- tda_gqap(lower(co2$F), lower(co2$D))
qap$assignment
```

    [1] 2 1 3

``` r
qap$cost
```

    [1] 36

``` r
# gqap's second output file: the multigraph under that permutation, with
# the flow and distance between each pair
qap$permuted
```

    2 1 2      1      2    1        5

    5 2 2      2      2    0        0
    6 2 3      2      3    7        1

    8 3 2      3      2    7        1

### 7.5.1.1 SAHN Algorithms

[`tda_cluster()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_cluster.md)
covers TDA’s clustering commands. The manual’s example dissimilarity
matrix is `cl1.dat`, the upper triangle of an 11 x 11 matrix, row by
row; `cl1.cf` runs `hcls` with `opt = 2`, complete linkage. The output
is the manual’s Box 3: at each level the two clusters merged, named by
their representative nodes.

Box 211hcls: complete-link clustering (cl1.cf) (id1.cf)

``` r
D <- scan(ex("cl1.dat"), quiet = TRUE)
dm <- matrix(0, 11, 11)
dm[lower.tri(dm)] <- D
dm <- dm + t(dm)
tda_cluster(dm, method = "hierarchical_single", options = list(opt = 2))$table
```

    8   8 33  1  5
    9   9 34  3  7

### 7.5.3.1 The Bond Energy Algorithm

### 7.6.1.1 Direct and Indirect Control

[`tda_gfcf()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_gfcf.md) is
`gfcf`, control in a directed valued graph – `gd3.dat` is a small
ownership network. With `sc = 49` (control at more than 49 per cent)
node 1 controls nodes 2 to 9, node 9 controls 1 to 8, node 3 controls 5;
the pair table of the manual’s Box 2 is the result’s `"pairs"`
attribute.

``` r
gd3 <- read.table(ex("gd3.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
```

### 7.6.1.2 Control

`gio` computes ownership shares in a directed valued graph: for each
pair, the direct share `A(i,j)` and the share including holdings held
through other nodes, `Y(i,j)`. `gd11.cf` runs it on `gd2b.dat`.

Box 221gio (gd11.cf)

``` r
gd2b <- read.table(ex("gd2b.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
tda_g_ownership(tda_graph(gd2b, directed = TRUE))$table
```

``` r
p <- tda_pl_graph(p, nodesB, edgesB)

p <- tda_pl_text(p, "Graph A", at = c(0.5, 3))
p <- tda_pl_text(p, "Graph B", at = c(6.5, 3))

plot(p)
```

### 8.3.2 Evaluation of Inclusion Functions

Chapter 8 is about set-valued data: a case is not a number but an
interval, and the answer is an interval too.
[`tda_evalfi()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_evalfi.md)
evaluates a function over interval arguments.

The manual’s box is `evalfi1`: the function’s inclusion over the
interval and its derivative’s, `derivative = TRUE`.

Box 225An inclusion function and its derivative (evalfi1)

``` r
tda_evalfi("sin(x)", x = c(0, 1))
```

       lower    upper 
    0.000000 0.841471 

``` r
tda_evalfi("sin(x)", x = c(0, 1), derivative = TRUE)
```

        lower     upper 
    0.5403023 1.0000000 

### 8.4.1 The gmin Command

[`tda_gmin()`](https://janmarvin.github.io/TDA/reference/tda_integrate.md)
finds the global minimum by subdivision. `start=` gives the search
interval, as `c(step, lower, upper)`; `tol_fe=` is the tolerance on the
function value within which a box is finally accepted. TDA 6.4p’s
default is 1e-10, and with it the box containing the minimum of sin(x)
on \[0, 10\] is only temporarily accepted (its lower bound is -1 to
sixteen digits, but not to ten); 1e-6 accepts it, giving one box with x
in \[4.71237, 4.71245\].

The manual’s box reports 39 iterations, 41 function evaluations and 77
inclusion evaluations. The program does not: running the manual’s
command file unchanged through TDA gives 19, 20 and 35, and so does the
call here. The manual is out of date on this box.

Box 226gmin

``` r
g <- tda_gmin("sin(x)", start = list(c(1, 0, 10)), use_derivatives = TRUE,
              tol_fe = 1e-6)
g$value
```

    [1] -1

``` r
g$boxes
```

      box accepted        width lower_f upper_f
    1   1        2 7.629395e-05      -1      -1

``` r
g$estimates
```

      box parameter    lower    upper
    1   1         x 4.712372 4.712448

``` r
# the counters TDA prints above the boxes
g$counts
```

               iterations           evaluations inclusion_evaluations            boxes_used 
                       19                    20                    35                     3 
          boxes_temporary        boxes_accepted 
                        1                     1

### 8.5.2 Interval-valued Variables

`iv(lower, upper)` is the interval-valued variable, the counterpart of
`Surv()` for this chapter.

``` r
id2 <- read.table(ex("id2.dat"))
id2$XL <- id2$V1 - 30L
id2$XH <- id2$V1 + 30L
tda_idf(~iv(XL, XH), data = id2)
```

### 8.6.1 Mean Values

The mean of an interval-valued variable is itself an interval: every
value in it is the mean of some admissible data set.

Box 230imean

``` r
tda_imean(~iv(XL, XH), data = id2)
```

    Call: tda_imean(~iv(XL, XH), data = id2)
